 179 │ def _parse_letter_version(letter, number):

 195 │ def _parse_local_version(local):

 206 │ def _cmpkey(epoch, release, pre, post, dev, local):
 207 │     # When we compare a release version, we want to compare it with all of the
 208 │     # trailing zeros removed. So we'll use a reverse the list, drop all the now
 209 │     # leading zeros until we come to something non zero, then take the rest
 210 │     # re-reverse it back into the correct order and make it a tuple and use
 211 │     # that for our sorting key.
 212 │     release = tuple(
 213 │         reversed(list(
 214 │             itertools.dropwhile(
 215 │                 lambda x: x == 0,
 216 │                 reversed(release),
 217 │             )
 218 │         ))
 219 │     )
 220 │ 
 221 │     # We need to "trick" the sorting algorithm to put 1.0.dev0 before 1.0a0.
 222 │     # We'll do this by abusing the pre segment, but we _only_ want to do this
 223 │     # if there is not a pre or a post segment. If we have one of those then
 224 │     # the normal sorting rules will handle this case correctly.
 225 │     if pre is None and post is None and dev is not None:
 226 │         pre = -Infinity
 227 │     # Versions without a pre-release (except as noted above) should sort after
 228 │     # those with one.
 229 │     elif pre is None:
 230 │         pre = Infinity
 231 │ 
 232 │     # Versions without a post segment should sort before those with one.
 233 │     if post is None:
 234 │         post = -Infinity
 235 │ 
 236 │     # Versions without a development segment should sort after those with one.
 237 │     if dev is None:
 238 │         dev = Infinity
 239 │ 
 240 │     if local is None:
 241 │         # Versions without a local segment should sort before those with one.
 242 │         local = -Infinity

 245 │         # the sorting rules in PEP440.
 246 │         # - Alpha numeric segments sort before numeric segments
 247 │         # - Alpha numeric segments sort lexicographically
 248 │         # - Numeric segments sort numerically
 249 │         # - Shorter versions sort before longer versions when the prefixes
 250 │         #   match exactly
 251 │         local = tuple(
 252 │             (i, "") if isinstance(i, int) else (-Infinity, i)

 315 │             |

 361 │             )

 364 │         self._specs = frozenset(_specs)

 367 │         return "<Specifier({0})>".format(repr(str(self)))

 370 │         return ",".join(["".join(s) for s in sorted(self._specs)])
 371 │

 399 │     def __contains__(self, item):
 400 │         # Normalize item to a Version, this allows us to have a shortcut for
 401 │         # ``"2.0" in Specifier(">=2")

 403 │         if not isinstance(item, Version):
 404 │             try:
 405 │                 version_item = Version(item)
 406 │             except ValueError:

 408 │                 # support identity comparison so do a quick check to see if the
 409 │                 # spec contains any non identity specifiers

 412 │                 # is on purpose as a non PEP 440 version should require
 413 │                 # explicit opt in because otherwise they cannot be sanely
 414 │                 # prioritized
 415 │                 if (not self._specs

 417 │                     return False

 429 │     def _get_operator(self, op):
 430 │         return getattr(self, "_compare_{0}".format(self._operators[op]))

 432 │     def _compare_compatible(self, prospective, spec):
 433 │         # Compatible releases have an equivalent combination of >= and ==. That
 434 │         # is that ~=2.2 is equivalent to >=2.2,==2.*. This allows us to
 435 │         # implement this in terms of the other specifiers instead of
 436 │         # implementing it ourselves. The only thing we need to do is construct
 437 │         # the other specifiers.

 440 │         # ignore post and dev releases and we want to treat the pre-release as
 441 │         # it's own separate segment.

 450 │         )

 453 │         prefix += ".*"

 455 │         return (self._get_operator(">=")(prospective, spec)
 456 │                 and self._get_operator("==")(prospective, prefix))

 460 │         if spec.endswith(".*"):

 462 │             # dot in between a release segment and a pre-release segment.
 463 │             spec = _version_split(spec[:-2])  # Remove the trailing .*
 464 │ 
 465 │             # Split the prospective version out by dots, and pretend that there
 466 │             # is an implicit dot in between a release segment and a pre-release
 467 │             # segment.
 468 │             prospective = _version_split(str(prospective))
 469 │ 
 470 │             # Shorten the prospective version to be the same length as the spec
 471 │             # so that we can determine if the specifier is a prefix of the
 472 │             # prospective version or not.
 473 │             prospective = prospective[:len(spec)]

 477 │             spec, prospective = _pad_version(spec, prospective)

 479 │             # Convert our spec string into a Version

 490 │     def _compare_not_equal(self, prospective, spec):
 491 │         return not self._compare_equal(prospective, spec)

 494 │         return prospective <= Version(spec)
 495 │ 
 496 │     def _compare_greater_than_equal(self, prospective, spec):
 497 │         return prospective >= Version(spec)

 499 │     def _compare_less_than(self, prospective, spec):

 503 │         return (prospective < Version(spec)

 505 │ 
 506 │     def _compare_greater_than(self, prospective, spec):
 507 │         # Greater than are defined as exclusive operators, this implies that
 508 │         # pre-releases do not match for the same series as the spec. This is
 509 │         # implemented by making >V imply !=V.*.
 510 │         return (prospective > Version(spec)
 511 │                 and self._get_operator("!=")(prospective, spec + ".*"))

 513 │     def _compare_identity(self, prospective, spec):

 517 │ _prefix_regex = re.compile(r"^([0-9]+)((?:a|b|c|rc)[0-9]+)$")

 520 │ def _version_split(version):
 521 │     result = []
 522 │     for item in version.split("."):
 523 │         match = _prefix_regex.search(item)
 524 │         if match:
 525 │             result.extend(match.groups())
 526 │         else:
 527 │             result.append(item)

 531 │ def _pad_version(left, right):
 532 │     left_split, right_split = [], []
 533 │ 
 534 │     # Get the release segment of our versions
 535 │     left_split.append(list(itertools.takewhile(lambda x: x.isdigit(), left)))
 536 │     right_split.append(list(itertools.takewhile(lambda x: x.isdigit(), right)))
 537 │ 
 538 │     # Get the rest of our versions
 539 │     left_split.append(left[len(left_split):])
 540 │     right_split.append(left[len(right_split):])
 541 │ 
 542 │     # Insert our padding
 543 │     left_split.insert(
 544 │         1,
 545 │         ["0"] * max(0, len(right_split[0]) - len(left_split[0])),

 547 │     right_split.insert(
 548 │         1,
 549 │         ["0"] * max(0, len(left_split[0]) - len(right_split[0])),
 550 │     )
 551 │ 
 552 │     return (
 553 │         list(itertools.chain(*left_split)),
 554 │         list(itertools.chain(*right_split)),
 555 │     )
